name: cvc
description: Track AI-assisted coding context alongside code changes. For the VS Code workflow, the extension reads GitHub Copilot chat session files stored locally by VS Code.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: CVC only runs repository discovery and local tools in trusted workspaces.

volute.lspPath.description: Machine-scoped custom path to the cvc-lsp binary. Leave empty to auto-detect from ~/.cvc/bin or PATH.

volute.cvcCliPath.description: Machine-scoped custom path to the cvc CLI binary. Leave empty to auto-detect from ~/.cvc/bin or PATH.

volute.cvcMcpPath.description: Machine-scoped custom path to the cvc-mcp binary. Leave empty to auto-detect from ~/.cvc/bin or PATH.

volute.suppressSetupPrompts.description: Suppress all setup and installation prompts on activation.

volute.trace.server.description: Traces communication with the Volute language server. Default is off. Verbose tracing can expose captured chat payloads in trace output.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Volute CVC
walkthroughs.description: Learn how to track your cognitive process alongside your code

steps.title: Review Local Capture and Sharing
steps.description:
Passive capture is off until you acknowledge the CLI notice. CVC may capture prompts, responses, exposed reasoning, and tool/context patches from this workspace’s locally stored chat sessions. Data is stored under the Git common directory’s `cvc/index.db` and is private by default. Sharing through hidden `refs/cvc/main` requires a separate remote-consent/share action. Scrubbing has limits, and content shared through Git may be permanent.

[Acknowledge in Terminal](command:volute.acknowledgePrivacyCapture) · [Refresh Privacy Status](command:volute.refreshPrivacyStatus)

media.markdown:
## Your choice

Opening the terminal does not enable capture. Complete the CLI's exact TTY challenge, then refresh status. CVC does not claim that data can never leave your machine: local capture stays local by default; a separately consented share can publish data to a remote.

steps.title: Check Your Setup
steps.description:
Volute CVC needs a few components to work. Let's make sure everything is installed.

[Check Setup](command:volute.checkSetup)

media.markdown:
## Components

- **CVC CLI** (`cvc`) — Handles local repo setup, commit linking, and optional terminal history checks
- **CVC Language Server** (`cvc-lsp`) — Powers the extension
- **CVC MCP Server** (`cvc-mcp`) — Not needed for this VS Code workflow. Required only for non-VS-Code AI clients.

steps.title: Welcome to Volute CVC
steps.description:
Volute CVC keeps the reasoning behind your AI-assisted changes next to the code. In VS Code, passive reading of locally stored GitHub Copilot chat sessions starts only after capture acknowledgement. Captured data is private by default; remote sharing requires separate consent.

[Learn More](https://github.com/meirka8/volute#readme)

media.markdown:
# Git, Augmented

Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code the way you normally do. Volute CVC reads GitHub Copilot chat session files stored locally by VS Code for this workflow, then shows the captured context in the timeline panel.

steps.title: Open a New Copilot Chat
steps.description:
Open GitHub Copilot Chat, start a new conversation, and work normally. After you acknowledge local capture, the watcher reads only this workspace’s Copilot chat session files stored locally by VS Code.

[Open Chat](command:workbench.action.chat.open)

media.markdown:
## Watcher-Based Workflow

The VS Code watcher is built for GitHub Copilot's chat storage format and reads the local `chatSessions` files that VS Code maintains for Copilot Chat. It does not rely on a separate CVC chat participant.

steps.title: Open the Volute Panel
steps.description:
Open the Volute panel in the Activity Bar after a Copilot exchange. You should see captured thoughts appear in the timeline automatically.

[Open Timeline](command:volute.timeline.focus)

media.markdown:
## Pending Thoughts

Thoughts first appear as pending. After you commit, they move into commit-linked history for that unit of work.

steps.title: Commit, Push, and Review
steps.description: When you run `git commit`, pending thoughts attach to that commit. After you push and open a PR, you can optionally inspect the same history in CVC Reviewer using a local GitHub PAT.

media.markdown:
## Optional PR Review

The local extension workflow is complete on its own. If you choose to use CVC Reviewer, it can read the same history beside a PR diff with a GitHub PAT; hosted integrations are optional.

scripts.compile: npm run clean && npm run check-types && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run clean && npm run check-types && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.test:unit: npm run compile && tsc --outDir dist --noEmit false && node --test dist/unit/**/*.test.js
